title: Killer robot talks, a tsunami warning gap and AI cameras on the court

stories.headline: Nations agree to keep working on 'killer robot' rules until 2028
stories.headlineZh: 各国同意在2028年前继续制定“杀手机器人”规则
stories.summaryZh: 日内瓦联合国会议决定继续讨论自主武器规则，但未承诺制定具法律约束力的条约。
stories.c1:
After more than a decade of talks, countries meeting at a United Nations conference in Geneva have agreed to keep working towards an international instrument on lethal autonomous weapons, the so-called "killer robots" that can select and attack targets without a human making the final decision. Under the deal announced on Saturday, the 128 participating countries have until 2028 to complete the task.

The outcome, however, falls short of what many had hoped for. Nearly 100 nations had pushed for the swift adoption of legally binding rules, but decisions under the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons require the consent of every member, and major arms producers, including the United States, Russia and Israel, resisted. Diplomats said Russian procedural objections forced some formal sessions to be cancelled, and the final wording was hammered out overnight.

Language proved to be a sticking point. According to Swiss diplomat Julien Thoeni, who chaired the conference, some countries objected to the word "negotiate", so the agreed text speaks instead of the "elaboration" of an instrument. That process is meant to determine which weapons should be prohibited outright under international humanitarian law and which might be permitted subject to regulation. Thoeni nevertheless hailed the result as a meaningful step, arguing that multilateral diplomacy can still deliver in a deeply divided world.

Campaigners were far less enthusiastic. The Stop Killer Robots coalition, which represents around 300 organisations, described the mandate as watered down, warning that it offers no clear path to binding rules even though AI systems that choose their own targets are already being used in combat. Human Rights Watch called the outcome disappointing, noting that the technology is advancing far faster than the diplomacy meant to rein in such weapons.
stories.b2:
Countries at a United Nations conference in Geneva have agreed to continue working on rules for lethal autonomous weapons. These are often called "killer robots" because they can choose and attack targets without a human making the final decision. The 128 countries now have until 2028 to finish the job.

However, many people wanted more. Nearly 100 countries asked for legally binding rules to be adopted quickly. But under this convention, every member must agree, and big weapons producers such as the United States, Russia and Israel were against the idea. Diplomats said objections from Russia led to some meetings being cancelled, and the final text was agreed overnight.

The exact words caused problems. Swiss diplomat Julien Thoeni, who chaired the meeting, said some countries did not accept the word "negotiate". The text now talks about the "elaboration" of an instrument. The process should decide which weapons are banned and which are allowed with regulation. Thoeni still called the result a meaningful step.

Campaign groups were less positive. The Stop Killer Robots coalition, which includes about 300 organisations, said the agreement was watered down and gave no clear route to binding rules. Human Rights Watch said the result was disappointing because the technology is moving much faster than the diplomacy.

vocab.en: to fail to reach a standard or expectation
vocab.example: The new stadium fell short of what fans had been promised.

vocab.en: the quick acceptance or approval of a rule, idea or technology
vocab.example: The scheme's swift adoption surprised even its designers.

vocab.en: having the force of law, so it must be obeyed
vocab.example: A verbal agreement can be legally binding in some situations.

vocab.en: to reach an agreement after long and difficult discussion
vocab.example: The two flatmates finally hammered out a cleaning roster.

vocab.en: an issue that prevents people from reaching agreement
vocab.example: Pay remained the main sticking point in the negotiations.

vocab.en: completely and immediately, not partly or gradually
vocab.example: Some councils want to ban e-scooters outright.

vocab.en: dependent on or controlled by something
vocab.example: All bookings are subject to availability.

vocab.en: involving three or more countries or groups
vocab.example: Climate change can only be tackled through multilateral cooperation.

vocab.en: to control or limit something more strictly
vocab.example: The government is trying to rein in spending before the election.

questions.q: Decisions under the Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons can be made by a majority vote.
questions.explain: 错误。原文说 decisions "require the consent of every member"，即需要全体成员同意，而不是多数通过。

questions.q: The agreed text refers to the "elaboration" of an instrument instead of using the word "negotiate".
questions.explain: 正确。原文：some countries objected to the word "negotiate", so the agreed text speaks instead of the "elaboration" of an instrument。

questions.q: Switzerland has offered to pay for the work on the new instrument.
questions.explain: 未提及。文中只说瑞士外交官 Julien Thoeni 主持了会议，没有提到任何国家出资。

questions.q: Why were legally binding rules not adopted quickly?
options: Most of the 128 countries rejected the idea of any rules
Every member must agree, and major arms producers resisted
The chair of the conference refused to hold a vote
The talks were cancelled after Russia left the conference
questions.explain: 原文：decisions ... require the consent of every member, and major arms producers ... resisted。因此需要全体同意而主要军火生产国反对。

stories.discuss: Should decisions about using lethal force ever be left to machines? Why do you think some powerful countries resist binding rules, and do you expect that to change in the future?

stories.headline: Tsunami warnings slower after staff leave remote Macquarie Island
stories.headlineZh: 麦夸里岛人员撤离后，海啸预警时间变慢
stories.summaryZh: 因禽流感担忧撤离人员后，麦夸里岛地震站停摆，地震探测时间约多出两分钟。
stories.c1:
Australia's ability to warn coastal communities of an approaching tsunami has been quietly weakened, according to internal documents obtained by the ABC. The seismic observatory on Macquarie Island, roughly 1,500 kilometres south-east of Tasmania, has been offline since staff were withdrawn from the remote research station in early October.

The withdrawal stemmed from concerns about a possible outbreak of H5 bird flu. Officials judged that expeditioners would suffer psychological strain if they had to spend months surrounded by dying and dead elephant seal pups, even though the staff themselves had said they were willing to stay. Once they left, the station lost power, and an attempt by Geoscience Australia to automate the observatory with solar panels was abandoned when strong winds made installation unsafe.

The consequences sound modest but could matter in practice. Detecting an earthquake in the region used to take about eight minutes; it now takes an estimated ten, adding roughly two minutes to tsunami alerts. Geoscience Australia concedes that detection will be slower and less sensitive for quakes south of Australia and New Zealand, yet maintains that warnings should still meet the required timeframe of around ten minutes. The move has also had knock-on effects for weather and wildlife monitoring.

Seismologists are less sanguine. The island sits on the boundary between the Pacific and Australian plates, a region that has produced at least nine earthquakes larger than magnitude 7.5 since 1900. Professor Hrvoje Tkalčić of the Australian National University described the silent station as a "major gap", pointing out that the nearest alternative is more than 1,000 kilometres away. Expeditioners are not expected to live on the island again until April or May 2028.
stories.b2:
Documents obtained by the ABC show that Australia now has less time to warn people about a tsunami. The earthquake observatory on Macquarie Island, about 1,500 kilometres south-east of Tasmania, has not worked since staff left the research station in early October.

The staff were removed because of worries about a possible bird flu outbreak. Officials thought it would be too stressful for them to live for months among dying and dead elephant seal pups, although the staff said they were happy to stay. After they left, the station had no power. Geoscience Australia tried to make the observatory work automatically with solar panels, but strong winds made this unsafe.

The change is small but important. It used to take about eight minutes to detect an earthquake in the area. Now it takes about ten, so tsunami alerts are around two minutes slower. Geoscience Australia says detection will be slower, but it still expects warnings to meet the required time of about ten minutes.

Scientists are more worried. The island is on the border between two tectonic plates, and the area has had at least nine very large earthquakes since 1900. One expert from the Australian National University called the station a "major gap". Staff are not expected to live there again until 2028.

vocab.en: to be caused by or come from something
vocab.example: Many of his worries stem from a lack of sleep.

vocab.en: mental stress caused by a difficult situation
vocab.example: Working night shifts for years can put enormous psychological strain on people.

vocab.en: to stop doing or trying to do something before it is finished
vocab.example: The match was abandoned because of heavy rain.

vocab.en: to admit, often unwillingly, that something is true
vocab.example: The coach conceded that the team had played poorly.

vocab.en: to keep saying that something is true, even if others disagree
vocab.example: She maintains that she never received the email.

vocab.en: the period of time within which something must happen
vocab.example: We need to finish the report within a tight timeframe.

vocab.en: an indirect result of an action or event
vocab.example: The train strike had a knock-on effect on city traffic.

vocab.en: hopeful and positive, especially in a difficult situation
vocab.example: Economists are less sanguine about next year's growth.

vocab.en: to tell someone a fact they may not have noticed
vocab.example: My tutor pointed out a mistake in my references.

questions.q: The Macquarie Island observatory has detected a tsunami during the past year.
questions.explain: 未提及。文章只说该站自十月起停摆，并未提到它近年是否探测到海啸。

questions.q: Geoscience Australia believes tsunami warnings should still meet the required timeframe.
questions.explain: 正确。原文：Geoscience Australia ... maintains that warnings should still meet the required timeframe of around ten minutes。

questions.q: The solar panels were installed on the island but did not produce enough power.
questions.explain: 错误。原文说自动化尝试 "was abandoned when strong winds made installation unsafe"，即太阳能板根本没有安装成功。

questions.q: How much longer does it now take to detect an earthquake in the region?
questions.explain: 原文：it used to take about eight minutes; it now takes an estimated ten, adding roughly two minutes to tsunami alerts。

stories.discuss: Was it right to put the wellbeing of staff ahead of scientific monitoring on Macquarie Island? How should governments balance human welfare against public safety in cases like this?

stories.headline: Parents push back against AI cameras at junior basketball games
stories.headlineZh: 家长反对在青少年篮球比赛中使用AI摄像头
stories.summaryZh: 澳大利亚篮协试行AI录像系统，逾1.3万人联署请愿，担忧儿童隐私与商业化。
stories.c1:
Basketball Australia's plan to film community games with artificial intelligence cameras has run into growing resistance from parents and campaigners, who argue that children's privacy is being treated as an afterthought. A petition launched last month by GetUp and the grassroots group Not All Clubs, calling on the sport's governing body to stop filming children, has now attracted more than 13,000 signatures.

The system, known as Hoops TV, was developed with the Israel-based company Pixellot. Smart cameras installed in stadiums record matches, including junior ones, and the footage, along with AI-generated statistics, is made available online to players and their guardians. It was trialled this week with associations in Darwin, the Illawarra region of New South Wales and Brisbane's northern suburbs, and a wider rollout is planned in the coming months. Crucially, games are recorded by default unless a parent or player objects.

Basketball Australia insists the technology is an exciting opportunity for the community game. Spokesman Tim Brenton argued that children are already being filmed informally at stadiums, and that Hoops TV simply allows such footage to be captured and managed in a more controlled way. As a non-profit, he added, the organisation ploughs back any revenue into basketball.

Critics remain unconvinced. Cyber-safety expert Susan McLean warned that any digital recording carries a risk of falling into the wrong hands, citing a spate of recent data breaches, and noted that several Victorian leagues have declined to take part. The petition also highlights an earlier Victorian trial in which a woman protected by a family violence intervention order was allegedly contacted by a man after her game was live-streamed. GetUp, meanwhile, fears that children's sport could end up being monetised through advertising.
stories.b2:
Basketball Australia wants to film community games with artificial intelligence cameras, but many parents and campaigners are against the plan. They say children's privacy is not being taken seriously. A petition started last month by GetUp and a group called Not All Clubs now has more than 13,000 signatures.

The system is called Hoops TV, and it was made with Pixellot, a company based in Israel. Cameras in stadiums record games, including junior games. Players and their parents or guardians can watch the videos and see AI statistics online. The system was tested this week in Darwin, the Illawarra region and northern Brisbane, and it will be used more widely in the next few months. Games are filmed unless a parent or player says no.

Basketball Australia says the technology is an exciting opportunity. Its spokesman, Tim Brenton, said people already film children at stadiums, and Hoops TV gives more control over the videos. He also said any money made goes back into basketball.

Critics are not convinced. A cyber-safety expert, Susan McLean, said any recording could be accessed by the wrong people, and that some Victorian leagues have refused to join. GetUp is also worried that children's sport could be used to make money from advertising.

vocab.en: to meet an unexpected problem or difficulty
vocab.example: The project ran into trouble when funding was cut.

vocab.zh: 事后才想到的事；次要考虑
vocab.en: something considered or added only after the main thing
vocab.example: Safety should never be an afterthought in building design.

vocab.en: coming from ordinary people rather than leaders
vocab.example: The campaign began as a small grassroots movement.

vocab.en: happening automatically unless you choose otherwise
vocab.example: Your phone backs up photos by default.

vocab.en: to reinvest profits into the same business or activity
vocab.example: The café ploughs back its profits into training staff.

vocab.en: to be obtained by someone who may misuse it
vocab.example: Keep your passwords safe so they don't fall into the wrong hands.

vocab.en: a large number of similar events happening close together
vocab.example: There has been a spate of burglaries in our street.

vocab.en: to politely refuse to do something
vocab.example: The minister declined to comment on the rumours.

vocab.en: to make money from something
vocab.example: Many apps monetise their users' data.

questions.q: Under Hoops TV, a game is filmed only if parents give written permission first.
questions.explain: 错误。原文：games are recorded by default unless a parent or player objects，即默认录制，需主动反对才不录。

questions.q: Several Victorian leagues have chosen not to take part in the scheme.
questions.explain: 正确。原文：several Victorian leagues have declined to take part。

questions.q: Pixellot has promised to strengthen its privacy settings for junior games.
questions.explain: 未提及。文中没有提到 Pixellot 作出任何回应或承诺。

questions.q: According to Tim Brenton, what is one benefit of Hoops TV?
options: It will make junior players more likely to turn professional
It will stop parents from filming games on their phones
It will be cheaper than paying professional camera operators
It allows footage of games to be captured and managed in a more controlled way
questions.explain: 原文：Hoops TV simply allows such footage to be captured and managed in a more controlled way。

stories.discuss: Should children's sport be filmed and analysed by AI by default? Who do you think should decide how such footage is used, and why?

stories.headline: Thousands rally against insurance rules threatening homebirth access
stories.headlineZh: 数千人集会反对威胁居家分娩的新保险规定
stories.summaryZh: 明年起私人执业助产士须购买保险方可接生，民众担心居家分娩服务大幅萎缩。
stories.c1:
Thousands of families, midwives and advocates took to the streets across Australia on Saturday, warning that new insurance rules threaten a "catastrophic collapse" in access to midwife-supported homebirths. Organisers Homebirth Australia said more than 12,000 people had registered for rallies at 26 locations, with hundreds gathering in Sydney's Hyde Park and outside the Northern Territory parliament in Darwin.

At the heart of the dispute is the end of an exemption, in place since 2009, that has allowed privately practising midwives to attend homebirths without private indemnity insurance. From 1 January, that exemption will be scrapped. The difficulty is that only about 5 per cent of the nation's 35,000 or so registered midwives are endorsed and therefore able to obtain the required cover, according to data from the health practitioner regulator.

Federal Health Minister Mark Butler has defended the change, describing it as a no-brainer that all health practitioners carry insurance, particularly for births, where the potential for serious harm is considerable. He noted that an insurance product has been developed and offered to midwives, and that health ministers agreed some 18 months ago to bring homebirth midwives into line with other professions.

Opponents counter that the available policy does not suit every midwife, and that regional women stand to lose the most, since some live hours from the nearest hospital and may have only one endorsed midwife in their area. Several speakers warned that the change could inadvertently push women towards freebirth, giving birth with no midwife or doctor present at all. The Australian College of Midwives has urged the government to come up with a more suitable policy.
stories.b2:
On Saturday, thousands of families, midwives and supporters joined rallies across Australia. They are worried that new insurance rules will make it much harder to have a homebirth with a midwife. The organisers, Homebirth Australia, said more than 12,000 people registered for rallies in 26 places, including Sydney and Darwin.

Since 2009, private midwives have been allowed to attend homebirths without private insurance. From 1 January, this exemption will end. The problem is that only about 5 per cent of Australia's roughly 35,000 registered midwives are endorsed and can get the insurance they will need.

The federal Health Minister, Mark Butler, supports the change. He said it is obvious that all health workers should have insurance, especially for births, because serious harm is possible. He said an insurance product is available to midwives, and that health ministers made this decision about 18 months ago.

People against the change say the insurance does not suit all midwives. They believe women in regional areas will be hit hardest, because some live hours from a hospital and have very few midwives nearby. Some speakers warned that more women may choose to give birth with no midwife or doctor at all. The Australian College of Midwives wants the government to create a better policy.

vocab.en: to protest publicly in large numbers
vocab.example: Students took to the streets to demand action on climate change.

vocab.en: at the most central or important part of something
vocab.example: Trust is at the heart of any good friendship.

vocab.en: to get rid of a plan, rule or system
vocab.example: The council scrapped its plan for a new car park.

vocab.zh: 不用多想的事；显而易见的选择
vocab.en: a decision that is very easy or obvious
vocab.example: Taking the train instead of driving in peak hour is a no-brainer.

vocab.en: to make something match a rule or standard
vocab.example: The new law brings our privacy rules into line with Europe's.
forms: bring homebirth midwives into line with

vocab.en: to reply to an argument with an opposing argument
vocab.example: When I said the plan was too expensive, she countered that it would save money later.

vocab.en: to be likely to lose something
vocab.example: Small shops stand to lose the most if the road is closed.

vocab.en: without intending to
vocab.example: I inadvertently deleted the whole folder.

vocab.en: to think of an idea, plan or solution
vocab.example: We need to come up with a better name for the project.

questions.q: The exemption for privately practising midwives was first introduced in 2009.
questions.explain: 正确。原文：an exemption, in place since 2009。

questions.q: Most registered midwives in Australia are already able to obtain the required insurance.
questions.explain: 错误。原文：only about 5 per cent of ... registered midwives are endorsed and therefore able to obtain the required cover。

questions.q: Mark Butler spoke at the rally in Sydney's Hyde Park.
questions.explain: 未提及。文章引用了 Butler 的观点，但没有说他是否出席集会。

questions.q: Why are women in regional areas expected to be hit hardest?
options: They may live hours from a hospital and have only one endorsed midwife nearby
They are not allowed to buy private health insurance
Regional hospitals have stopped offering birth services
The new rules apply only outside the capital cities
questions.explain: 原文：regional women stand to lose the most, since some live hours from the nearest hospital and may have only one endorsed midwife in their area。

stories.discuss: How should governments balance patient safety with people's freedom to choose how they receive care? Do you think rules like this make birth safer or riskier overall?

dialogue.title: After the Flat Inspection
dialogue.setting: Two friends compare notes on the footpath after inspecting a two-bedroom flat in Brunswick on a Saturday morning.
dialogue.settingZh: 周六上午，两个朋友在不伦瑞克看完一套两居室公寓后，站在人行道上交换看法。

lines.name: Ines
lines.en: Well, that was a bit of a mixed bag, wasn't it?
lines.zh: 嗯，这房子有好有坏，对吧？

lines.name: Kofi
lines.en: Yeah, the photos definitely did it a few favours, I reckon.
lines.zh: 是啊，我觉得照片确实把它拍得好看多了。

lines.name: Ines
lines.en: The second bedroom was tiny. You'd barely squeeze a single bed in there.
lines.zh: 第二间卧室太小了，勉强才能塞进一张单人床。

lines.name: Kofi
lines.en: True, but the kitchen's been done up, and the light's lovely in the mornings.
lines.zh: 没错，但厨房翻新过，而且早上采光很好。

lines.name: Ines
lines.en: Did you notice that damp patch on the bathroom ceiling, though?
lines.zh: 不过你注意到浴室天花板上那块潮湿的印子了吗？

lines.name: Kofi
lines.en: I did. That's a bit of a red flag, to be honest.
lines.zh: 注意到了。说实话，那有点让人担心。

lines.name: Ines
lines.en: And there must have been thirty people traipsing through. It's so competitive.
lines.zh: 而且来看房的人起码有三十个，竞争太激烈了。

lines.name: Kofi
lines.en: Tell me about it. Half of them had their applications ready on the spot.
lines.zh: 可不是嘛。一半人当场就把申请材料准备好了。

lines.name: Ines
lines.en: Should we put in an application anyway, just to keep our options open?
lines.zh: 要不我们还是先递个申请，给自己留条后路？

lines.name: Kofi
lines.en: I'm on the fence. It's close to the tram, but the rent's a stretch.
lines.zh: 我还拿不定主意。离电车站近，但租金对我们来说有点吃力。

lines.name: Ines
lines.en: We could ask the agent whether they'd fix the damp before we move in.
lines.zh: 我们可以问问中介，入住前能不能把潮湿问题修好。

lines.name: Kofi
lines.en: Good call. If they're cagey about it, that tells us everything we need to know.
lines.zh: 好主意。如果他们支支吾吾，那就说明一切了。

lines.name: Ines
lines.en: Right, let's sleep on it and decide by tomorrow night.
lines.zh: 好，那我们先考虑一晚，明晚前做决定。

lines.name: Kofi
lines.en: Sounds like a plan. Coffee first, though? I'm running on empty.
lines.zh: 就这么定了。不过先喝杯咖啡吧？我快没电了。
